To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TNF-α levels are associated with APC system impairment and that combined TNF-α/ThP determination may be used as a predictive tool for VTE risk assessment in patients with mCRC.

TNF-α levels and APC functionality were increased and decreased in mCRC patients, respectively, and an inverse correlation was observed among them, suggesting that TNF- α might be responsible for APC impairment.

TNF-α, an inflammatory cytokine released from tumor cells or from the host immune response to cancer, may be responsible for the APC system dysfunction observed in patients with metastasized colorectal cancer, and that the combined determination of TNF-α levels and the APC system function could be a useful tool in the risk assessment of venous thrombosis in patients with metastatized colorectal cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between TNF- α levels and defects in APC system as a predictor of VTE in metastatic colorecral cancer (mCRC) patients.
the possible role of TNF-α levels in the pathogenesis of VTE in cancer patients.

the role of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) in the activation of the coagulation system and its possible association with the development of venous thrombotic events in patients with metastasized colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF-α is a marker of APC resistance, and that both markers are predictive of VTE in CRC patients undergoing chemotherapy.
TNF-α levels could be used as a biomarker to predict VTE events in mCRC patients.
TNF-α levels and APC functionality should be considered as independent predictors of VTE in metastatic colorectum cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNF-α is associated with APC system abnormalities in mCRC, and that combined TNF-α/ThP determination might be useful in the risk assessment of VTE in these patients.
TNF-α levels and abnormalities in the activated protein system are associated with VTE risk in patients with metastasis colorectal cancer.
TNF-α levels could be used to identify mCRC patients with a high risk of developing VTE, and that these patients could be considered for prophylaxis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TNF-α levels are associated with the risk of VTE in patients with mCRC, and that combined ThP/TNFA determination may be useful for the risk stratification of VTE in this clinical setting.
the combination of APC system and TNF-α determination could represent a promising tool for the risk stratification and management of thromboembolic complications in mCRC patients.
